title: How could I set up a skill so that it drains HP?

posts.author: wyrmoffastring
posts.body: Basically, I want the skill to drain MP normally, but if the character doesn't have enough MP, to drain HP instead. Is there a way to do this?

posts.author: NoNameWithoutAName
posts.body:
Absolutely!
You could do this by having the skill trigger a common event that contains a conditional statement comparing the value you're draining to the current MP of the caster. You'll need to assign/update variables ahead of time, to represent the caster's actor ID and their current MP in the conditional statement.
Plugins such as
Yanfly Skill Core
, which lets you control a lot of this stuff through note tags in the skills/actor databases, will make this much more efficient.
If you do use Yanfly's skill core plugin, I think I've got a script you can drop in the skill's notebox to set it up without needing any common events... but I don't know where it's at in my notes, and I've been away from RMMV for much too long to write it from memory with any amount of accuracy XD so that'll have to wait

Try this in your skill's notebox. It should just need the battle core
Code:
<JS Pre-Damage>
target._prevMp = target.mp;
</JS Pre-Damage>

<JS Post-Damage>
if (target._prevMp < value){
  target.gainHp(target._prevMp - value);
  user.gainHp(value - target._prevMp);
}
</JS Post-Damage>

Click to expand...
Ah, now that's a different mechanic. When you said it drains MP and should drain HP if there's not enough MP, I believed you were using an MP Drain skill and you wanted the skill to drain the target's HP if they didn't have enough MP.
For costs, you can use this:
Code:
<JS MP Cost>
cost = user.mp >= skill.mpCost ? skill.mpCost : 0;
</JS MP Cost>
<JS HP Cost>
cost = user.mp >= skill.mpCost ? 0 : 500;
</JS HP Cost>
If the battler can pay the MP cost, it's their MP cost. If they can't, the MP cost is waived and it'll have an HP cost instead. Change the 500 in the bottom one for whatever that HP cost should be.

posts.author: rpgLord69
posts.body:
Note that the VS tags you were given it's either MP or HP (if you can't pay all MP) cost. Your plugin it's HP cost for the part that your actor can't pay as MP.
EDIT: I think you should also edit that mp reduction, because if it's like that, the value can show a negative for a moment, before it updates to 0.
